questions.question: Which display is usually suitable for comparing counts across categories?
What does a histogram usually group into intervals?
Which display emphasizes median, quartiles, and spread?
What does a scatterplot show?
choices: Only the total number of observations
Pairs of values for two quantitative variables

questions.question: What is a frequency in a data table?
choices: The number of observations in a value or category
The width of a graph's axis

questions.question: Which display commonly shows how a quantity changes over time?
A pie-chart category covers one-fourth of the circle. What percent does it represent?
Why should a graph's axis labels include measurement units when relevant?
choices: Units identify what the numerical scale represents
Units make every graph show causation
Units determine the number of data points

questions.question: Why can a bar graph with a truncated vertical axis exaggerate differences?
choices: It changes the original data values
It proves the categories are unrelated
It can make small differences look proportionally large
It removes the need for a scale

questions.question: A frequency table lists 6 students walking, 9 riding buses, and 5 cycling. How many students are represented?
A table lists 6 students walking, 9 riding buses, and 5 cycling. What fraction ride buses?
Why does a histogram differ from a category bar graph?
choices: Histogram bars represent numerical intervals rather than separate named categories
Bar graphs must have connected points

questions.question: A scatterplot trends upward from left to right. What association is suggested?
A box plot has median 12. What does that mark represent?
choices: The middle value or middle-value average of the ordered data

questions.question: Why should graph comparisons use consistent scales when judging visual differences?
choices: Different scales can create misleading apparent differences
Matching scales make the data identical

questions.question: A line graph shows values 10, 14, 13, and 18 across four consecutive days. Between which days is the greatest increase?
A table has intervals 0–9 with frequency 4, 10–19 with frequency 7, and 20–29 with frequency 3. Which interval has the highest frequency?
A chart labels two categories 40% and 70% of the same whole, with no overlap. What is wrong?
A scatterplot shows ice-cream sales and swimming attendance increasing together. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Swimming necessarily causes every ice-cream sale
They are associated, but the plot alone does not establish causation
There can be no other influencing variable

questions.question: A graph reports averages but omits sample sizes. What important information is missing?
choices: How many observations support each average
Whether every observation equals the average
The identity of the graph's font
